why: Nearly every command checks out. The named files exist: the bin, cli.test.js, the README, test.yml and package-lock.json for `npm ci`. Argument lists, the printf setup, the process substitution in `diff <(...)`, the grep patterns, `npm test --workspace packages/jsonl-lint` and the gh/jq calls are all valid. The problem is Check 4, `git diff --exit-code b74bddb HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`. It hard-codes the revision `b74bddb` and calls it "the commit before this work". Nothing in the repository facts gives this commit's hash, so there is no basis for that SHA. If it isn't the real base commit, git exits with "bad revision" instead of comparing the file. A command that compared against the PR's base (e.g. `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`) would have run as written. Because the run depends on an unsupported literal, I can't confirm every command works in this repository.
